notes:
NO TRANSMISSION CHANNEL is imposed by Portuguese law for B2B invoicing today — established by direct reading of Decreto-Lei n.º 28/2019, de 15 de fevereiro (original publication text, Diário da República, 1.ª série, N.º 33, retrieved as a PDF via curl from files.diariodarepublica.pt, checked 2026-09-13), which governs invoice handling across the whole of Portuguese tax law (IVA, IRC, IRS).

Article 12.º nº 1 sets out the principle: the electronic transmission of an invoice is a FACULTY subject to the recipient's agreement, never an obligation or an imposed channel: « As faturas e demais documentos fiscalmente relevantes podem, mediante aceitação pelo destinatário, ser emitidos por via eletrónica. » — translation: invoices and other tax-relevant documents MAY, subject to acceptance by the recipient, be issued electronically. The verb is « podem » (may), not « devem » (must): electronic issuance itself remains optional and consensual, unlike the French (PDP) or Italian (SdI) regimes, which remove this choice from the parties. No platform, no network, no intermediary is named anywhere in this article or in the rest of chapter II (« Emissão de documentos ») of the same decree-law.

Article 3.º lists the only PROCESSING MEANS (« meios de processamento ») recognized — a question of PRODUCING the document, not of its transmission channel: « Os sujeitos passivos devem assegurar que as faturas e demais documentos fiscalmente relevantes sejam processados por uma das seguintes formas: a) Programas informáticos de faturação, incluindo aplicações de faturação disponibilizadas pela Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (AT); b) Outros meios eletrónicos, nomeadamente máquinas registadoras, terminais eletrónicos ou balanças eletrónicas; c) Documentos pré-impressos em tipografia autorizada. » — none of these three routes is a transmission channel in the sense of this catalog (KSeF, SdI, PDP…): they are means of GENERATING the document, independently of how it subsequently reaches the customer.

SOFTWARE CERTIFICATION REGIME — DISTINCT FROM A CHANNEL, AND NOT SATISFIED BY THIS PRODUCT TODAY: article 4.º nº 1 imposes, on certain taxpayers, the EXCLUSIVE use of software certified by the AT — a requirement on invoicing SOFTWARE, never on the sending channel: « os sujeitos passivos com sede, estabelecimento estável ou domicílio em território nacional e outros sujeitos passivos cuja obrigação de emissão de fatura se encontre sujeita às regras estabelecidas na legislação interna nos termos do artigo 35.º-A do Código do IVA, estão obrigados a utilizar, exclusivamente, programas informáticos que tenham sido objeto de prévia certificação pela AT, sempre que: » with, at point a), the threshold that triggers this obligation: « Tenham tido, no ano civil anterior, um volume de negócios superior a € 50 000 ou, quando, no exercício em que se inicia a atividade, o período em referência seja inferior ao ano civil, e o volume de negócios anualizado relativo a esse período seja superior àquele montante; ». Invoicerr is NOT certified by the Portuguese AT today: for any Portuguese taxpayer whose turnover exceeds this threshold, this CERTIFIED SOFTWARE obligation applies and is not currently satisfied by this product — a fact distinct from the channel question addressed by this file, never to be confused with it, and which remains a genuine product gap for the Portuguese market independently of anything this file may say about channels.

B2G — A LEGALLY DISTINCT REGIME ALREADY ESTABLISHED IN PRINCIPLE, BUT NOT COVERED HERE: unlike B2B, invoicing in the execution of Portuguese PUBLIC CONTRACTS IS legally mandatory in principle: art. 299.º-B nº 1 do Código dos Contratos Públicos (introduced by Decreto-Lei n.º 111-B/2017, de 31 de agosto, Diário da República, 1.ª série, N.º 168, transposing directive 2014/55/EU; text likewise retrieved as a PDF via curl from files.diariodarepublica.pt, checked 2026-09-13) provides: « No âmbito da execução de contratos públicos, os cocontratantes são obrigados a emitir faturas eletrónicas, as quais, sem prejuízo dos requisitos exigidos na legislação fiscal, contêm imperativamente os seguintes elementos, sempre que aplicáveis: » — translation: in the execution of public contracts, the contracting parties ARE OBLIGED to issue electronic invoices. Nº 3 refers the FORMAT to the European standard: « O modelo de fatura eletrónica é o estabelecido pela norma europeia respetiva aprovada pela Comissão Europeia e publicitada no portal dos contratos públicos. », and nº 5 refers the designation of the CHANNEL and the « aspetos complementares » to a separate portaria, not identified nor read by this task: « A regulamentação dos aspetos complementares da faturação eletrónica é feita por portaria dos membros do Governo responsáveis pelas áreas das finanças e das obras públicas. » WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the B2G obligation does indeed exist, in principle, in Portuguese law. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED BY THIS TASK: the identity of the concrete platform/channel this portaria imposes (presumably the eSPap/FE-AP platform cited in professional literature, never verified here against an official document) — that is precisely the work of `b2g-routing/data/pt.json`, which does not exist yet: this absence is NOT filled by this file, which deliberately addresses only the general question, outside public procurement.

WHAT THIS READING COULD NOT ESTABLISH, HONESTLY: (1) the text of Decreto-Lei n.º 28/2019 cited above is that of its ORIGINAL PUBLICATION (15 February 2019) — the viewer of « legislação consolidada » from diariodarepublica.pt is a client-side application that serves no raw text on a plain HTTP request (it answers with the application shell regardless of the URL requested), so the accuracy of articles 3.º, 4.º, and 12.º cited here has not been reconfirmed against an official consolidated text incorporating any later amendments; several recent professional sources (accounting firms, software vendors, 2020-2026) nonetheless continue to describe this same recipient-consent rule and this same €50,000 threshold without mentioning any change, which makes it reasonably reliable without being direct documentary proof; (2) a reform widely discussed by the Portuguese professional press for 2027 (obligation of a structured format « CIUS-PT » with a qualified electronic signature, on pain of refusal of payment by the State) was not verified against a primary source by this task — its own wording ("refusal of payment BY THE STATE") strongly suggests it extends the B2G regime of art. 299.º-B above rather than introducing a general B2B channel, but this remains an inference rather than a direct reading, to be checked against the relevant Lei do Orçamento do Estado before being encoded anywhere in this repository.
